title: testkit newSession adoption stalled
note: Confirmed numbers: root-package NewSession( 922 lines in 219 files, newSession(t 833, llm.NewClient() 1044; session_dod_definition_test.go 65 vs 0, session_config_test.go 40 vs 1, session_model_test.go 34 vs 3; testkit_test.go:21-27 states the intent. Severity lowered to medium: pure test-code ergonomics with no drift-induced bug, and the 'about -4,000 net' estimate is optimistic given per-test config variation.

title: Coverage-wave test files organized by sprint label with stale line-number comments
note: Core confirmed: session_tools_jobs_covtest2_test.go:18-20 cites session_tools_jobs.go lines 298-300 but clearDescendantReceiverWatchByID is at session_tools_jobs.go:370; 388 lines in 50 files carry '(lines N-M)' references; TestS3Cov_ 59, TestS2Cov_ 31 confirmed. Size is overstated or counted differently: a find over agent/** for names containing cov/coverage gives 247 files / 47.4K lines (including subpackages); root-only cov/covtest/s4cov names give 133 files / 28K lines. Not the claimed 211/42.1K. 'Merge into subject files' of ~28-47K lines is a very large churn for a cosmetic gain.
revised_fix_plan: Do the cheap parts: strip '(file.go lines N-M)' parentheticals mechanically and rename wave-prefixed tests/helpers by AST rename. Defer file merging until files are otherwise touched. Do not delete tests (coverage floor agent 94.7 needs Jesse approval).

title: Nil-receiver and trivia tests pad coverage and pin over-defensive production guards
note: Evidence real: 272 Test*Nil* funcs, 95 'var x *Session' decls; nil_guards_covtest_test.go:19,31 pin the same error text via err.Error() != literal (also a copy-oracle violation); cov_s2_getters_test.go:24-28 weak oracles (ContextPressure() < 0); session_attention_cov_test.go:95-110 no-assertion nil tests. But the fix of deleting production nil guards is not safe to assume: guards on *Session methods are defensive against partially constructed sessions and removal needs per-guard caller analysis; plan itself notes a floor decision. Severity lowered to low as the harm is padding, not drift.
revised_fix_plan: Phase 1 only: delete assertion-free tests and >=0 style oracles, and collapse duplicate NilSession/EmptyID pairs, keeping guards. Phase 2 (removing production guards) only per guard with proven-unreachable callers and Jesse's approval of the coverage-floor change.

title: Fuzz targets that ignore their input and replay about 60 TestXxx funcs; seed100 files named for a percentage
note: Partly right. session_init_seed100_exact_fuzz_test.go:26-33 confirmed: f.Add(byte(0)), f.Fuzz(func(t, _ byte)) replaying existing Test funcs (e.g. TestInitPlugins_UnknownHookEventWarnsLoudly). But all 17 *seed100* files are //go:build evenerfuzz, so the range_a/b/c/d, more, final helpers are fuzz-lane-only code, not duplicates of untagged tests, and runAgentJobsSeed100 (jobs_seed100_fuzz_test.go:24) is invoked by a registered fuzz target with real text input. Deleting them would drop coverage the fuzz lane provides, contrary to the claim that they add nothing. Only the Test-func-replay targets are redundant.
revised_fix_plan: Delete only fuzz targets whose body is a pure replay of untagged Test funcs (session_init_seed100_exact first). For helper-based seed100 files, rename to subject names and keep them; verify the coverage union in CI before deleting anything.

title: Duplicated wait/poll helpers and avoidable real sleeps
note: Helpers confirmed: waitForCondition (poll_test.go:18), waitFor (session_lossless_events_test.go:785, 5 call sites), waitForTreeCount/waitForDriveCount (tree_counter_test.go:20,34 identical except message). 1100ms sleeps at jobs_activity_incremental_fold_test.go:190,237 and foldcache_test.go:174,240,277,531 confirmed. But subagent_intent_report_test.go:255 is a deliberate hold 'past the activity publication window' tied to a production real-clock window; replacing with agenttest.NewFakeClock is only valid if production reads an injectable clock there, which was not shown.
revised_fix_plan: Replace waitFor/waitForTreeCount/waitForDriveCount with waitForCondition; use os.Chtimes for the mtime sleeps; leave the 1200ms sleep unless the activity window is shown to use an injectable clock.
